speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe the exact location and nature of your sudden onset abdominal pain, and tell me if you have a history of gallstones, appendicitis, or similar conditions.

speaker: Patient
text: 74-year-old male. The patient presents with sudden onset of abdominal pain around the umbilicus 16 hours ago, with recent history of hospitalization for an acute myocardial infarction a week ago. Reports several episodes of bloody loose bowel movements. Denies vomiting.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds like an emergency. Given your recent heart attack and bloody stools, could you describe the color of the blood (bright red vs. black/tarry) and tell me if you have felt any fever or chills? Please tell me immediately if you feel dizzy, faint, or if your abdomen is rigid to the touch.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe abdominal pain. I also have Bloody loose bowel movements, No vomiting, Sudden onset.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Mesenteric Ischemia.

The combination of sudden onset periumbilical pain, bloody stools, and a recent myocardial infarction strongly suggests bowel ischemia from low-flow states. I am requesting immediate CT angiography of the abdomen and pelvis to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: CT_Abdomen_Pelvis_with_contrast; REQUEST IMAGES.
